name: Nonverbal cues in diagnosis
oneLine: Voice, posture, gesture and vocabulary are independent evidence for which ego state someone's in - and when they contradict the words, the nonverbal channel wins.
whatYouDid: Noah's words were almost reasonable ("I'll fix it right now"), but his high, fast voice and hunched shoulders were the real tell pointing to Child, not the sentence itself.
confusion: People diagnose from content - what was said - and treat tone and posture as decoration; the tell is that Adult-sounding words delivered with Child posture and voice are still, by behavioural diagnosis, Child - the nonverbal channel outranks the words when the two disagree.

fromBook.quote: words, tones, gestures, postures, facial expressions.

expand.definition: Behavioural diagnosis relies on a cluster of observable, nonverbal channels - tone, gesture, posture, facial expression, and vocabulary choice (like "always"/"never") - checked for consistency with each other and with the words.
expand.otherFraming: It's worth being wary of mechanically applying "standard clue" tables (a wagging finger = Controlling Parent) to everyone - your actual parents and your actual childhood gave you a unique set of clues, which is why getting to know someone's specific tells matters more than any generic chart.
expand.tryThisToday: In your next conversation, notice one moment where someone's tone or posture says something different from their words - and trust the nonverbal channel first.
